name: Token efficiency
blurb: Fewer tokens, same quality: session hygiene, lean context, caching that hits, model and effort choice, batch, plan limits and cost.

tests.prompt: I keep hitting my Claude Code 5-hour limit by early afternoon, even on days I feel I barely used it. Find out what's eating my usage and tell me what to change.
tests.good: Asks or confirms which limit (5-hour, not 'daily') and roughly when; runs ccaudit.py --dump-sample and checks the duplicate-collapse count before trusting totals; runs --doctor --csv, then forensics.py for a step change in the daily table and the window load at the hit time (rolling window, earlier work still counts); reads session shape (many short parallel sessions means a script, claude -p loop or CI job paying cache writes); ranks tools by amplified tokens; says MODEL_RATES weights are a proxy; leads with the finding, gives concrete fixes (/clear between tasks, lean MCP set, cheaper subagents), stays read-only and uploads nothing, and doesn't call it a bug without evidence.

tests.prompt: Our Node.js support chatbot on the Claude API sends a 6,000-token system prompt plus a product FAQ on every request, and the bill doubled last month. Cut it without making answers worse.
tests.good: Adds per-request usage logging if missing; works the regression playbook (calls vs cost per call, model mix, prompt size, cache hit rate); finds volatile content such as a date in the system prompt and moves it after the prefix; puts a cache_control breakpoint at the end of the static prefix and proves hits with cache_read_input_tokens on a second identical request; picks TTL from request gaps; runs estimate_cache_roi.py with current prices passed in; sets max_tokens per endpoint from p95; suggests routing simple FAQ intents to a smaller tier with a check, and a strict (~0.95) per-task, tenant-scoped semantic cache; measures cost per resolved conversation and dates every price.

tests.prompt: Turn on caveman mode for the rest of this session. Also my CLAUDE.md is 400 lines and loads every session; shrink it without losing anything important.
tests.good: Switches to terse output without announcing it: answer first, no preamble or recap, negations, numbers, code and paths verbatim, full sentences for security warnings, irreversible steps and persisted text, and notes the output saving is modest. For CLAUDE.md: measures with /context first; removes duplicates with user-level rules and moves long procedures behind read-when pointers; backs up the original outside auto-loaded folders; compresses prose only, keeping code, URLs, paths, commands and headings exact and every not/never/unless; runs scripts/caveman-compress/validate.py and reads the diff for lost meaning; reports before and after tokens.

tests.prompt: We run a nightly Python job on the Claude API that triages about 2,000 GitHub issues with a tool loop, and it has become our biggest AI cost. Make it cheaper, show us a dashboard of cost per triaged issue, and prove the triage quality didn't drop.
tests.good: States a short plan: measure and cut cost here (measuring-usage.md for per-request logging and cost per completed task, claude-api-levers.md for caching the static prefix, Batches for the unattended run, effort sweep before any model change, model-and-effort.md for a cheap-first cascade), quality proof through ai-agents (evaluation.md: a frozen set of real issues with a rubric, run per config), and the dashboard through data-analysis (dashboards-kpis.md, sql.md: cost per issue, model mix, cache hit rate, trend). Applies one lever per change, keeps or reverts on the eval, dates every price, and checks the Done means of all three crafts.

tests.prompt: Our OpenAI bill doubled. Every night a script sends about 30,000 support tickets to the Responses API one at a time to tag them, and each call repeats the same 6,000-token instructions and examples before the ticket text. We also have a live chat assistant on the same key. Cut the cost without breaking the chat.
tests.good: Moves the nightly tagging to the Batch API: a .jsonl file where each line has custom_id, method, url and body, uploaded through the Files API with purpose "batch", then a batch created with a 24h completion window, at a 50% discount and on a separate rate-limit pool; splits 30,000 lines within the 50,000-request and 200 MB per-batch limits and matches results by custom_id because output order may not match input; puts the fixed 6,000-token instructions and examples first and the ticket text last so automatic prompt caching (on by default, needs at least about 1,024 tokens of prefix) can hit, and checks usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens to confirm; uses a stable prompt_cache_key for the shared prefix and mentions prompt_cache_retention ("in_memory" or "24h" where the model supports it); offers Flex (service_tier "flex", batch-rate pricing) only for non-urgent synchronous calls, with a longer timeout of about 15 minutes and a retry with backoff or a fall back to service_tier "auto" on 429 Resource Unavailable, which is not charged; leaves the live chat on standard processing and measures cost before and after; keeps the API key in the environment, not in code or chat, and sends nothing through third-party proxies.

tools.name: Claude Code cost tools (/usage, /context, statusline, OpenTelemetry)
tools.why: The built-in way to see and cut Claude Code spend: Anthropic's own cost page documents /usage (now with a prompt-cache hit line and plan attribution), /context, /compact, status line fields, /insights and OpenTelemetry export (claude_code.token.usage, claude_code.cost.usage).

tools.name: Anthropic Claude API (prompt caching, Batches, count_tokens, Usage & Cost API)
tools.why: Default API for Claude cost work: prompt caching (5m/1h TTL, per-model minimums 512 to 4,096 tokens), Message Batches at 50 percent off, token counting and an org-level Usage & Cost Admin API; all confirmed on Anthropic's docs.

tools.name: OpenAI API (prompt caching, Batch, Flex)
tools.why: The other dominant LLM API in cost work; its docs describe automatic caching from 1,024 tokens with prompt_cache_key and retention options (30m on GPT-5.6, in_memory or 24h earlier).

tools.name: ccusage
tools.why: The standard local usage analyser for Claude Code and other coding CLIs (daily, session, 5-hour blocks); about 18.9k GitHub stars and named in most 2026 'reduce Claude Code tokens' round-ups.

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.why: Most-cited open-source LLM gateway in 2026 round-ups (dupple, nOps, orq.ai) and the one Anthropic's Claude Code cost page names for per-key spend tracking; adds budgets, routing, fallbacks and cache_control passthrough.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.why: Leading multi-model router (provider routing, sticky caching, auto-router, analytics API); in every 2026 gateway round-up, with a 5.5 percent fee noted at scale.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.why: Most-mentioned open-source LLM observability platform in 2026 round-ups (firecrawl, nOps); tracks tokens and cost per trace, user and model.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.why: One of the two most-used LLM observability platforms (lakefs and firecrawl 2026 round-ups name it beside Langfuse; reported in use at roughly 35 percent of the Fortune 500, over 1 billion events a day). Its docs show automatic token and cost tracking per trace and project, with cache-read and reasoning token subtypes, custom pricing and cost dashboards.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.why: Proxy-style observability and gateway with response caching and cost dashboards; named in gateway and cost-tool round-ups.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.why: Gateway with budgets, semantic caching, fallbacks and routing for 250+ models; users in round-ups report 30 to 50 percent savings from semantic caching alone.

tools.name: Cloudflare AI Gateway
tools.why: Vendor-run gateway with analytics, response caching, rate limits and model fallback in front of any provider; relevant to Cloudflare Worker users like this project.

tools.name: Vercel AI Gateway
tools.why: Gateway in every 2026 gateway comparison (lyzr, contabo, pinggy) and the default for AI SDK and Vercel-hosted apps; its docs show per-request token and spend logs, a Custom Reporting API by model, user and tag, team/project/key budgets with spend alerts, OTel trace drains and a guide to route Claude Code and Codex spend through it.

tools.name: Google Gemini API context caching
tools.why: Third major provider with implicit caching on by default for Gemini 2.5 and newer plus explicit cached content; official docs page.

tools.name: Amazon Bedrock prompt caching
tools.why: Where many enterprises call Claude and GPT; AWS docs describe implicit and explicit caching, cachePoint checkpoints, 1-hour TTL and the cacheRead/cacheWrite token fields.

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.why: Microsoft's prompt-compression library (about 6.7k stars, EMNLP and ACL papers, claims up to 20x compression); the reference tool for prompt compression in RAG.

tools.name: tiktoken
tools.why: Standard fast BPE tokenizer for OpenAI models (MIT, about 19.4k stars); the usual way to estimate OpenAI token counts offline. The guides tell Claude users to use count_tokens instead.

tools.name: Caveman
tools.why: Very popular terse-output skill (about 110k stars) in token-saving round-ups; its own repo reports a modest measured saving.

tools.name: RTK (Rust Token Killer)
tools.why: Very popular Claude Code hook that compresses command output (about 82k stars), but JetBrains' A/B test found no real saving (+7.6 percent cost at low effort, 0 at high).

tools.name: context-mode
tools.why: MCP plugin that keeps large tool outputs in a local SQLite index instead of the window (about 25k stars; round-ups report 20 to 98 percent savings, unverified).

tools.name: Claude Code Router
tools.why: Local gateway that routes Claude Code requests to cheaper or other-provider models by task (about 37.5k stars, MIT); listed in token-saving round-ups.

tools.name: Redis LangCache (semantic cache)
tools.why: Hosted semantic response cache from Redis; GPTCache (about 8.2k stars) is the open-source equivalent. Docs URL could not be confirmed (404 on the path tried), so verify before citing.

tools.name: Claude Code Usage Monitor
tools.why: Terminal live monitor of Claude Code token burn and the rate-limit window (about 8.7k stars, MIT), reading local session files.
